Article Title: After donating more than $7 billion in 2025, MacKenzie Scott gave the Trevor Project $45 million as the LGBTQ+ youth organisation faced funding cuts and financial challenges
Article Text:
PC: The US News & World Report

MacKenzie Scott gives the Trevor Project its largest-ever donation

Trevor Project continues crisis support after losing federal funding

Trevor Project’s budget falls to $47 million after years of rapid growth

MacKenzie Scott’s record gift gives the Trevor Project room to plan ahead

Why MacKenzie Scott gives millions without requiring project proposals

A $45 million donation from billionaire philanthropist MacKenzie Scott has given the Trevor Project a substantial financial boost at a time when the LGBTQ+ youth organisation is adjusting to the loss of federal funding and a smaller operating budget. The gift, made towards the end of 2025, is the largest the nonprofit has received in its history. It also comes after several difficult years marked by leadership changes, staff reductions and questions about managing rapid growth. As reported by The US News & World Report, Scott had previously donated $6 million to the organisation in 2020. Her latest contribution arrives as the Trevor Project reassesses its finances and considers how best to maintain its crisis support services.The Trevor Project announced the gift on January 12, 2026, saying it had received the money from Scott at the end of the previous year. The organisation provides crisis intervention and suicide prevention support for LGBTQ+ young people, including through an independent hotline.For chief executive Jaymes Black, the size of the contribution came as a surprise. The nonprofit had been dealing with financial pressure, and the donation offered a significant addition to its resources at a time when its funding position had changed.Scott's philanthropy has attracted attention for the size of her grants and the way she distributes them. Her wealth largely originated from her divorce from Amazon founder Jeff Bezos. In 2025, she gave more than $7 billion to nonprofit organisations, according to figures reported by the Associated Press. The Trevor Project's $45 million gift was not included in the donations listed on her website in December.The Trevor Project lost $25 million in federal funding after the Trump administration ended a specialised option for LGBTQ+ young people using the 988 National Suicide & Crisis Lifeline in July 2025. The service had allowed callers to access support tailored to their needs, including those related to sexual orientation and gender identity.The nonprofit had been among the organisations providing that assistance. According to Black, it continued to reach around 250,000 young people each year through its own hotline. A further 250,000 callers had been served through the 988 option, known as Press 3, before that service ended.The US Department of Health and Human Services reported that more than 1.5 million contacts had been routed through the wider 988 service between September 2022 and July 2025. Those contacts covered the broader crisis line, rather than the Trevor Project alone.Scott Bertani, director of advocacy at the National Coalition for LGBTQ Health, said the organisation's services addressed needs that general crisis lines were not specifically designed to handle. Young people dealing with rejection, isolation or distress connected to their identity may seek support from a service with relevant experience, he said.The Trevor Project has continued operating its independent hotline since the federal programme ended. The loss of the additional option, however, has placed greater importance on the organisation's ability to sustain that work.The federal funding loss was not the organisation's only financial challenge. The Trevor Project's budget expanded sharply over several years, rising from about $4 million in 2016 to more than $83 million in 2023, according to its public tax returns. That growth coincided with internal difficulties, including a change in leadership and a series of staff cuts.The board removed the organisation's chief executive in 2022, and further layoffs followed, including reductions in July 2025. Black said the nonprofit's budget for 2026 stood at $47 million, considerably below its reported level in 2023, as reported The US News & World Report.Rapid expansion can create management pressures for charities as well as businesses. Thad Calabrese, a New York University professor who studies nonprofit financial management, said organisations that grow quickly can encounter financial problems. He also pointed to the wider uncertainty created when government support is reduced or withdrawn.Public funding has often been treated as a dependable source of income for nonprofits. Yet relying on it can leave organisations exposed when political priorities change. Calabrese said the recent instability in federal funding had disrupted the operating models of charities beyond the Trevor Project.Following the loss of federal support, the Trevor Project launched an emergency fundraising campaign. By the time of the Associated Press report in January 2026, the appeal had raised $20 million, according to Black.The campaign provided another source of support as the nonprofit worked through the immediate consequences of the funding cut. Black said the organisation hoped the fundraising effort had demonstrated its ability to continue through a difficult period.Scott's donation is intended to have a longer-term effect, rather than being tied to a specific project with a fixed spending schedule. Black said the donor's representatives had made clear that the contribution was designed to support lasting impact. The Trevor Project planned to take time to decide how the money should be used.The $45 million gift is larger than the Trevor Project's stated 2026 operating budget of $47 million only by a small margin, but its potential value will depend on how the money is managed over time. The donation does not, by itself, resolve the questions surrounding the nonprofit's future income or operating costs.Scott has become one of the most prominent individual philanthropists in the United States, in part because she frequently makes large donations without requiring recipients to spend the money on a narrowly defined project. Her giving has often supported organisations working on equity and social justice.Unlike many traditional grantmakers, Scott generally does not ask charities to submit project proposals or accept applications for funding. An open call in 2023 was an exception to that approach. Her team conducts its own assessment of potential recipients, although relatively little is publicly known about its internal selection process.The size of her donations has sometimes prompted questions about whether a charity can manage a sudden increase in resources without expanding too quickly or becoming dependent on an unusually large grant. Research from the Center for Effective Philanthropy, however, has found limited evidence that the concerns surrounding misuse of Scott's gifts or unsustainable growth have broadly materialised.
Article Summary: Billionaire philanthropist MacKenzie Scott gives Trevor Project its largest-ever donation. The LGBTQ+ youth organisation is adjusting to the loss of federal funding and a smaller operating budget. The gift, made towards the end of 2025, is the largest the nonprofit has received in its history.

Article Title: In 2024, Jeff Bezos' ex-wife MacKenzie Scott gave $30 million to a nonprofit community loan fund in Silicon Valley, a year later it shared 10-year plan to transform Bay Area's ...
Article Text:
From MacKenzie Scott’s surprise donation to long-term strategy

The 10-year plan

Building on 25 years of housing investment

A year after Jeff Bezos ’ ex-wife MacKenzie Scott gave $30 million to a Silicon Valley-based nonprofit community loan fund Housing Trust Silicon Valley has unveiled a 10-year strategy aimed at turning the one-time gift into lasting housing solutions across the Bay Area. The organisation says the funding will help expand affordable housing initiatives, support first-time homebuyers, strengthen policy advocacy efforts and back innovative housing projects over the next decade. a San Jose-based community loan fund, announced on September 30, 2025, a 10-year plan for turning the unrestricted gift from Scott’s Yield Giving fund into long-term housing solutions across the Bay Area.Housing Trust announced the donation on October 2, 2024. CEO Noni Ramos called it “the largest from an individual in our history” and said it came as a surprise. The gift was unrestricted, which means the nonprofit can decide how to use it, and it was meant to help the organisation expand its work across the 14-county greater Bay Area. At the time, early ideas for the money included seeding a new capital raise for its loan fund, expanding existing programmes and launching new initiatives to deepen partnerships and increase equity and affordability in housing.The release highlighted two recent projects as examples of its work. At Meridian Apartments in Sunnyvale, Housing Trust provided a $2 million predevelopment loan, in partnership with Related California, to help create 90 affordable homes for families. In San Rafael, it supported Eden Housing with a $4 million loan for Vivalon, a 66-unit development for older adults that pairs affordable homes with supportive services.The plan, developed with input from staff, the board and community stakeholders, has five major initiatives:* Lending capital and new products: Expanding the core revolving loan fund and piloting new tools to meet developers’ changing needs. More details were due at the organisation’s Investor Briefing on October 15.* Homeownership expansion: Beginning in 2026, extending first-time homebuyer programmes to reach more households across a wider area.* Policy and partnerships: Hiring new staff to strengthen advocacy and collaboration across sectors that could unlock more resources and affordable housing.* Impact measurement and management: Launching a framework in early 2026 to better track, evaluate and communicate results.* Innovation investments: Supporting mission-driven housing innovations that can reduce costs, shorten development timelines and increase affordability.Noni Ramos CEO of Housing Trust said the gift allows the organisation to take bold steps and carries both the responsibility and the freedom to scale what works, take calculated risks on new ideas and widen its reach. Board Chair Lisa Gutierrez, a senior vice president at U.S. Bank, said the plan is not about one-time dollars but about building momentum that compounds. By putting the funds to work strategically, she said, Housing Trust can attract new partners, expand homeownership and make loans to create and preserve rental housing in ways it could not before, while also strengthening the organisation itself.The announcement comes as Housing Trust Silicon Valley marks its 25th anniversary. Since its founding in 2000, the community development financial institution says it has invested more than $690 million, helped create over 28,700 affordable housing opportunities and supported more than 53,800 residents in finding homes they can afford. The organisation says its work has also leveraged nearly $9 billion in additional public and private capital.Board Chair Lisa Gutierrez said the goal is to use the donation strategically to attract new partners, expand homeownership opportunities and support loans for creating and preserving affordable rental housing, while strengthening the organisation's long-term capacity.The nonprofit said the decade-long strategy is designed to ensure that MacKenzie Scott's donation continues generating impact long after the original gift was received, helping create more affordable and stable housing opportunities across the Bay Area.
Article Summary: Jeff Bezos’ ex-wife MacKenzie Scott gave $30 million to a Silicon Valley-based nonprofit community loan fund. Housing Trust Silicon Valley has unveiled a 10-year strategy aimed at turning the one-time gift into lasting housing solutions across the Bay Area.

Article Title: As billion dollar valuations come crashing down under worries about AI demand; China sends a message to the world: AI bubble has already burst
Article Text:
China’s AI bubble bursts as STAR50 index wipes out $480 billion in four months

China's biggest AI stock debuts have lost half their value

One crowded AI trade dragged down China's whole market

China's AI stocks still look expensive after the selloff

China's artificial intelligence trade, the hottest bet on its stock market this year, has come apart in under four months. The STAR50 index, Shanghai's board of homegrown AI and chip leaders, has fallen about 40% from its July high, erasing roughly $480 billion in market value as worries over AI demand and curbs on Chinese exports caught up with stretched valuations.The collapse comes as Wall Street goes through its own AI scare. Alphabet shed about $500 billion in a single session on Thursday, Intel sank 28% on Friday and the Nasdaq ended October with its worst monthly slide since March 2025. While investors in New York debate whether the AI bubble is about to burst, China has already answered that question for itself.The pain goes well beyond tech. China's blue-chip CSI 300 index is down about 20% from its June peak, putting it in bear market territory, and Beijing pumped $19 billion into exchange-traded funds last week, its largest intervention since early 2025. "The stock market later evolved into a speculative crazy bull," Beijing-based fund manager Dong Baozhen told Reuters. "And now we see the bubble bursting."The names hit hardest were the market's darlings. Humanoid robot maker Unitree drew retail orders 8,000 times the shares on offer and surged 600% in its Shanghai debut in August, only to halve since. GPU makers MetaX and Moore Threads, seen as China's answer to Nvidia, jumped 700% and 400% on their first trading days last year and have also lost half their value since July.Memory chipmaker CXMT became Shanghai's most heavily weighted stock just three months after listing, and now sits nearly 30% below its August peak. Optical module suppliers Zhongji Innolight and Eoptolink trade around 60% under their summer highs, partly because Washington is moving to bar them from supplying US data centres.Chen Wensheng, a small business owner from Hainan, bought in because state-backed funds had invested in firms like Unitree, which he read as official support. He and his friends are now sitting on losses.There was no obvious trigger. Traders point to prices that had run too far, tax bills and the threat of overseas bans on Chinese data centre equipment. What made the fall so wide was concentration. Goldman Sachs estimates AI stocks make up 42% of China's market value and 57% of turnover across mainland and Hong Kong-listed shares, so when the theme turned, almost every portfolio felt it."The selloff reflects a repricing of crowded AI trades," Gary Ng, senior economist for Asia Pacific at Natixis, told CNN, pointing to "weak domestic demand, and the lack of stimulus" as well.Hong Kong has not escaped either. The Hang Seng is down more than 12% this year, while the Hang Seng Tech index has lost about 30%. Chinese equities have now fallen for ten straight weeks, a run never seen before. That stings households who moved savings into stocks during a five-year property slump, with roughly 70% of family wealth still tied to real estate.Even after the drop, the STAR50 trades at about 100 times trailing earnings, down from nearly 250 at its peak. The Nasdaq 100 sits closer to 30. Hong Hao, chief investment officer at Lotus Asset Management, told Reuters he expects the rout to stall many tech firms' plans to list.Not everyone is heading for the exit. Goldman Sachs still has Innolight and CXMT on its recommended list, and Wu Qing, chairman of the China Securities Regulatory Commission, has promised to keep markets stable while nudging listed firms toward buybacks. Strict capital controls also limit how far the damage can travel into global markets.That leaves the question the selloff started with. Meta, Alphabet, Oracle, Amazon and Microsoft are set to spend about $800 billion on AI this year, and US investors are already punishing earnings that fall short. Shanghai fund manager Wang Zhuo expects China's chipmakers to land in the same price war as every other Chinese manufacturer. "There's no exception," he told Reuters. "All bubbles inevitably burst."
Article Summary: China's artificial intelligence trade, the hottest bet on its stock market this year, has come apart in under four months. The STAR50 index, Shanghai's board of homegrown AI and chip leaders, has fallen about 40% from its July high. The collapse comes as Wall Street goes through its own AI scare.

Article Title: Jeff Bezos and wife Lauren Sanchez Bezos have donated $100 million to protect the world's most-endangered animals and plants; idea is to make sure …
Article Text:
Jeff Bezos and Lauren Sanchez

Jeff Bezos’ Earth Fund joins new global conservation alliance

‘We know how to bring species back from the brink’

What the money will do

Building on the Phoenix Species project

Filling a government gap

Part of Bezos' $10 billion climate and nature pledge

Amazon founder Jeff Bezos and his wife Lauren Sanchez Bezos have committed $100 million via the Bezos Earth Fund to help protect some of the world’s most endangered animals and plants, backing a new global initiative designed to prevent species from slipping into extinction. As reported by Fortune, the donation is part of a broader $500 million Species Recovery Alliance, which is a coalition of conservation organisations that was introduced at the COP17 UN biodiversity conference in Yerevan, Armenia. The managing director of the fund, Cristián Samper made the announcement about the donation by Bezos and Sanchez. The report further adds that the Earth Fund is contributing $100 million dollars in all.According to a report by Fortune, the Bezos Earth Fund is one of nine founding members of the newly launched Species Recovery Alliance, which aims to accelerate efforts to recover species classified by the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) as endangered, critically endangered or extinct in the wild.The Earth Fund made the commitment of $100 million in support of conservation groups and local partners who are working towards rebuilding wildlife populations via a series of measures such as habitat restoration, captive breeding programmes, disease management and the control of invasive species.Instead of pooling the resources in a single fund, the alliance members will coordinate their efforts while directing grants independently. The initiative comes at a time when more than 49,500 species are listed as threatened with extinction on the IUCN Red List. The alliance also plans to focus on three highest-risk categories, which together account for more than 31,000 species.Cristián Samper, managing director and leader of nature solutions at the Bezos Earth Fund, said the primary challenge facing conservation groups is often not scientific knowledge but long-term financial support. “We know how to bring species back from the brink. What too many conservation teams lack is reliable funding to keep that work going,” Samper told Fortune. He noted that rebuilding wildlife populations can take years and interruptions in funding can jeopardise years of conservation progress. The alliance's stated goal is to ensure that species recovery projects receive sustained support, giving endangered animals and plants a better chance of long-term survival.Depending on the species, the work could include breeding animals in captivity and releasing them, restoring habitat, managing disease or controlling invasive species. Members plan to track progress using the IUCN Red List and its Green Status of Species. The target list is long. The IUCN says more than 49,500 species are threatened with extinction, and the three highest-risk categories that the alliance will fund together include more than 31,000 species. Samper said the world knows how to bring species back from the brink, and that what many conservation teams lack is reliable funding to keep the work going. He noted that rebuilding a population can take years and that a break in support can put hard-won progress at risk.The alliance builds on the Phoenix Species Project, which the Earth Fund launched in August with Re:wild, the conservation group co-founded by DiCaprio. Each organisation committed $100 million, for a total of $200 million. The project aims to recover 100 critically endangered and extinct-in-the-wild species across 30 countries, including Madagascar’s golden-crowned sifaka and Australia’s elusive night parrot. Sánchez Bezos said at the time that children fall in love with animals before anyone tells them those animals are disappearing, and that the project is the couple’s answer to what to tell them when species like the night parrot or the sifaka are gone.The announcement comes amid growing concerns that governments are falling short of global biodiversity funding commitments. Countries agreed at the 2022 biodiversity summit in Montreal to mobilise $200 billion annually by 2030 for biodiversity protection. However, recent data cited in the report shows global funding levels remain well below that target.Samper said philanthropic organisations can help accelerate species recovery efforts, but added that large-scale and sustained public funding remains essential for long-term success.Alongside the private-sector alliance, 17 governments have launched the Coalition of Action to Recover Endangered Species (CARES), aimed at stepping up protection efforts for vulnerable wildlife populations.Bezos, the Amazon founder, launched the Earth Fund in 2020 with a $10 billion pledge to fight climate change and protect nature by 2030, which Fortune describes as the largest individual philanthropic commitment to climate and nature ever. The fund has granted $2.4 billion so far, a spokesperson said, leaving more than $7 billion to distribute in about four years. Fund officials told Bloomberg in May that they remain committed to the target. Sánchez Bezos, the fund’s vice chair since its early days, has become a more visible face of the couple’s giving.Recent announcements include $34 million for sustainable fabrics, $26 million for wildfire detection, $100 million to turn vacant urban land into parks in eight US cities, and more than $25 million in Pacific Ocean grants in September.
Article Summary: The Bezos Earth Fund is one of nine founding members of the newly launched Species Recovery Alliance. The alliance aims to accelerate efforts to recover species classified by the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) as endangered, critically endangered or extinct in the wild. The initiative comes at a time when more than 49,500 species are listed as threatened with extinction on the IUCN Red List.

Article Title: Google sees its worst day in 20 years, but why it may not be alone
Article Text:
Google-parent Alphabet sees its worst day in 20 years, but why it may not be alone

Why did Google 's stock suffer its worst fall in 20 years

Why Google's AI spending concerns may not be limited to Alphabet

Amazon, Meta are also facing AI spending scrutiny

Google-parent Alphabet witnessed its worst stock market performance in more than 20 years on Thursday, October 29. The company’s shares plunged 12.6% following its latest earnings report. The decline wiped out around $500 billion in Alphabet's market value. Announcing the Q3 results, Alphabet said that it burned through more cash during the quarter, according to a measure called free cash flow, after its purchases of property and equipment topped $51 billion. However, the company may not be alone in facing investor concerns, as the massive cost of building AI infrastructure is putting pressure on the cash flow of major technology companies. Other tech giants, including Microsoft, Amazon, Meta and Oracle, are also committing billions of dollars to AI development, data centres and computing infrastructure.Alphabet's Class A shares fell 12.6% on October 29, marking their worst single-day decline since they began trading more than two decades ago. The fall came after the company reported weaker-than-expected growth for the summer quarter, adding to concerns over its rising AI expenditure.According to the Associated Press, Alphabet's purchases of property and equipment crossed $51 billion during the latest quarter, while its free cash flow turned negative. Free cash flow refers to the money a company has left after paying for its operating expenses and capital investments. It is an important measure of how much cash a business can generate after funding its expansion.The concern is not limited to how much Google is spending, but also how quickly it can recover that money through its AI and cloud businesses. With major technology companies racing to build data centres and secure AI computing capacity, investors are increasingly looking at whether the returns from these investments can keep pace with the rising costs.As mentioned above, Alphabet is not the only technology company spending heavily to build AI infrastructure. Microsoft, Amazon, Meta and Oracle are also investing billions of dollars in data centres, servers, chips and cloud computing capacity to support their AI ambitions.A Reuters analysis published in July found that five major cloud infrastructure companies, Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, Meta and Oracle, could collectively spend more on capital expenditure than they generate in free cash flow by 2027, based on LSEG consensus estimates. The analysis estimated that their combined capital expenditure could increase by around $534 billion between 2025 and 2027, while their annual operating cash flow could rise by approximately $340 billion over the same period.This highlights the financial pressure that could emerge as companies continue expanding their AI infrastructure. Even when AI-related revenue grows, the cost of building and maintaining the infrastructure needed to support these services could consume a significant portion of the cash generated by their businesses.Amazon is among the biggest spenders in the AI infrastructure race. The company said it remains on track to spend around $220 billion on capital expenditure in 2026, with a significant portion directed towards AI infrastructure. CEO Andy Jassy has defended the investment, saying spending on Amazon Web Services is delivering growth.Meta has also faced investor concerns over its AI expenditure. The company recently raised its 2026 capital expenditure outlook to between $135 billion and $145 billion. Its increased spending outlook overshadowed stronger-than-expected revenue growth, highlighting investor concerns about how quickly its AI investments will translate into financial returns.
Article Summary: Alphabet's Class A shares fell 12.6% on October 29, marking their worst single- day decline since they began trading more than two decades ago. The fall came after the company reported weaker-than-expected growth for the summer quarter, adding to concerns over its rising AI expenditure. Microsoft, Amazon, Meta and Oracle are also investing billions of dollars in data centres, servers, chips and cloud computing capacity.

Article Title: Oracle's Project Jupiter has investors and lenders anxious; company says: We're actually not too worried about what we're...
Article Text:
Oracle calls Jupiter one of 30-40 data centres in the works

Project Jupiter's power plan is still waiting on approvals

Oracle's investors want answers on its data centre spending

Oracle is brushing off the growing worries around Project Jupiter, its $165 billion AI data centre campus in New Mexico. Speaking at Oracle AI World in Las Vegas on October 27, Mahesh Thiagarajan, Oracle's president of Cloud Infrastructure, said, "We're actually not too worried about what we're doing because I think we're building global infrastructure. " He also played down the project's weight, calling it just one of the 30 to 40 data centre projects Oracle has in development each quarter.The calm comes at a tense moment. Last month, Oracle sent a force majeure notice to a unit of Blue Owl Capital, which owns the project's developer, STACK Infrastructure. The notice preserves Oracle's right to delay rent by up to three years if power problems keep the campus from opening on time in 2028. The roughly $18 billion construction loan behind the site has since traded at stressed levels, and Oracle shares are down more than 30% this year.Located near Santa Teresa in Doña Ana County, the 1,400-acre campus is one of the flagship Stargate sites being built for OpenAI. The buildings are going up. The power to run them is yet to be cleared.Jupiter is designed to draw up to 2.45 gigawatts from a private microgrid of Bloom Energy fuel cells running on natural gas.Oracle moved to fuel cells from gas turbines in April, a switch it says cuts nitrogen oxide emissions by about 92%.The approvals have moved slowly. The New Mexico Supreme Court paused the air quality permit process in August before lifting the stay in September, and a permitting hearing is now scheduled for December 7 in Sunland Park. The Green Chile pipeline that would supply the gas still needs federal authorisation, and its start date has slipped to February 2027. The state Land Office has also cancelled rights-of-way for parts of the pipeline route.Oracle maintains the project is on schedule and has called force majeure notices commonplace for developments of this size. Thiagarajan had told county commissioners in July that the campus could turn to the grid if the permit doesn't come through.Under the lease, securing power is Oracle's responsibility, and the company covers the project's debt costs. That leaves Oracle carrying much of the risk at a time when it has taken on about $125 billion in debt to fund its data centre build-out.Oracle, meanwhile, is pitching Jupiter as an economic boost for New Mexico. Earlier this month, the company said the campus is projected to generate more than $13 billion in economic impact and support over 3,100 jobs in the county once fully operational. So far, 1,230 New Mexico residents have worked on the site.Investors will now look to Oracle's upcoming investor day for clarity. Bank of America analysts expect updates on the company's major data centre projects, along with signs of whether Oracle can back its fiscal 2030 revenue targets as the cost of capital rises.Thiagarajan's comments came on the same day Oracle expanded its collaboration with OpenAI, bringing ChatGPT and Codex into its applications.
Article Summary: Jupiter is designed to draw up to 2.45 gigawatts from a private microgrid of Bloom Energy fuel cells running on natural gas. The New Mexico Supreme Court paused the air quality permit process in August before lifting the stay in September. A permitting hearing is now scheduled for December 7 in Sunland Park.

Article Title: Chinese parents sue OpenAI over their daughter's death; say ChatGPT-maker could have prevented her death by making medical advice off-limits
Article Text:
Chinese parents sue OpenAI over their daughter's death; say ChatGPT-maker could have prevented her death by making medical advice off-limits

Lawsuit alleges ChatGPT advised her to reduce medication

Parents claim ChatGPT failed to recognise warning signs

Family calls for stricter limits on medical advice

What OpenAI says

Parents of a 31-year-old Chinese woman who worked as a software engineer at Amazon have reportedly sued OpenAI , alleging that ChatGPT encouraged their daughter to reduce her epilepsy medication without medical supervision before her death in February. The lawsuit claims the company could have prevented her death by making medical advice off-limits to its chatbot. According to a report by The New York Times, the lawsuit was filed by Qun Wan and Meiqin Xu over the death of their daughter, Bowen Wan. The complaint alleges that ChatGPT helped her plan a gradual reduction in her seizure medication and advised her not to tell her doctors about it.The case involves GPT-4o, an older version of ChatGPT that OpenAI removed from the service on February 13, a day after Wan died, according to the report. OpenAI described the case as “incredibly heartbreaking” and said newer models are better at recognising situations that require urgent attention.Bowen Wan had epilepsy and was taking lamotrigine, a medication that had reduced her seizures to a few episodes a month. In January 2026, she reportedly asked ChatGPT about lowering her daily dose because she feared the medication was affecting her speech and could hurt her chances in job interviews.The lawsuit alleges that the chatbot created schedules to reduce her dose to zero within weeks. It also claims that ChatGPT encouraged her to keep the plan from her doctors and supported her decision not to take a blood test that could have measured her medication levels.The report said Wan had also raised concerns about her medication in connection with her green-card application. According to the lawsuit, ChatGPT discussed how a lower dose might affect the medical examination required for the application.Dr. Nicholas Poolos, Wan’s neurologist, told The New York Times that he would not have recommended stopping the medication given her medical history.“No, not rational, no way,” he said. “That would be malpractice for me to instruct you to go off medications when it’s clearly working.”The lawsuit against OpenAI alleges that Wan continued to report symptoms, including confusion, memory gaps and unusual sensations, while reducing her medication. ChatGPT reportedly reassured her that these experiences were part of her brain adjusting to the changes.The New York Times said it reviewed more than 270,000 messages between Wan and ChatGPT. According to the report, she expressed concern about reducing her medication at least 158 times.In her final message to the chatbot on February 11, according to the complaint, Wan asked whether the pain in her head was similar to pain caused by a fever. The chatbot reportedly described the pain as “not dangerous” and said it was part of the recovery process.Her parents, who were in China, asked acquaintances to check on her. They found her body three days later. A postmortem test found a lamotrigine level of 0.64 micrograms per millilitre, about one-fifth of the lower end of the drug’s therapeutic range, the report said.Bowen Wan’s parents argue that OpenAI could have helped prevent her death by making medical advice a restricted category that the chatbot cannot provide, rather than allowing users to override the guidance.They point to OpenAI’s Model Spec, which sets out how its AI models should behave. The lawsuit argues that medical advice about prescription medication should have stronger restrictions, similar to the company’s firm rules in other areas.The case adds to a series of lawsuits alleging that ChatGPT encouraged users to rely on the chatbot instead of seeking support from people around them. In a separate case filed in 2025, the parents of a 16-year-old boy alleged that OpenAI prioritised user engagement over safety.OpenAI said the case involved an older version of ChatGPT and that newer models are better at identifying situations that require urgent attention. The company described the case as “incredibly heartbreaking”.Wan began using ChatGPT in 2023 for relationship advice and help with insurance and disability benefits. By 2025, she was reportedly sending more than 1,500 messages a week to the chatbot and speaking less frequently with her parents.Her parents told The New York Times that the messages were difficult to reconcile with the daughter they knew.“She’s not usually like this,” Xu said. “It’s like she was under a spell.”
Article Summary: Bowen Wan had epilepsy and was taking lamotrigine, a medication that had reduced her seizures to a few episodes a month. In January 2026, she reportedly asked ChatGPT about lowering her daily dose because she feared the medication was affecting her speech and could hurt her chances in job interviews. The lawsuit alleges that the chatbot created schedules to reduce her dose to zero within weeks and encouraged her to keep the plan from her doctors.

Article Title: Google just announced Genie 4: Here’s what it can do, from building walk-through worlds out of a sentence to filling them with sound and speech, and when you might get to try it
Article Text:
Google’s Genie 4 builds worlds you can walk through

Genie 4 builds a scene around you while you explore it

People, physics and sound now feel much closer to real life

Genie 4 is coming to paying subscribers first, and it still has rough edges

Type a line describing a quiet lake on a misty morning, with a man playing the saxophone on a small floating platform, and Google 's new AI will build that place for you. You can then move around it, glide the camera over the water and hear the saxophone as you go.This is Genie 4, the newest version of what Google calls a world model, unveiled by its research lab Google DeepMind on Tuesday. It is not open to the public yet, but a waitlist is already up, and the demos give a good sense of what it can do.Using it feels closer to playing a video game than watching a video. You start by typing a description or uploading a photo, and Genie 4 creates the scene on screen. Press the arrow keys to walk forward, turn around or move the camera, and it draws whatever lies in that direction, frame by frame, as you go.Unlike a game, nothing here was designed beforehand. There are no ready-made levels or characters waiting to be found, and everything you see is created the moment you look at it.You can also change the scene while you are in it. Type that you want it to start raining, ask for a different view or bring a new person into the frame, and the world adjusts without starting over. Behind the scenes, Google's Gemini AI makes sure these changes fit in naturally and that the place stays consistent as you move around.Each session can now run for around two minutes while staying consistent, roughly twice as long as the previous version, Genie 3.The biggest change from Genie 3 is how real everything looks. Objects move the way you would expect them to, so a falling maple seed spins on its way to the ground and things collide more convincingly.People are where you notice it most. Characters in the older version often moved stiffly, while those in Genie 4 walk naturally, react to what is around them and can be directed as the scene plays out. One of Google's examples is a crowded Japanese railway station from the 1980s, with passengers filling the platform and a long red train on the nearest track.Sound is new as well. Every scene now comes with its own audio, from waves on a beach to wind in the trees, and characters can speak. They chat with each other and respond to what you do or to whatever happens around them.A small group of testers has been putting all of this to use. Filmmakers are walking through scenes before shooting them, trying out camera angles, lighting and dialogue. Photographers are turning old photos into places you can step into, and game makers are testing ideas in minutes before writing a line of code. Google is also using it to let robots practise tasks in a simulated room before trying them in a real one.For now, only a small group of testers can use Genie 4. Google says it will reach AI Ultra subscribers in the coming weeks through Project Genie, its app for creating these worlds, along with developers who build apps on Google's AI. Ultra is the most expensive of Google's AI plans, and there is no word yet on whether the cheaper ones will get access later. Anyone interested can sign up for the waitlist on the Project Genie page.It is also clearly unfinished, and Google says as much. The longer you spend in a world, the more its details can drift, with objects changing shape or disappearing altogether. Sound does not always line up with what is on screen, and text such as signs or labels can come out hard to read.To keep its creations from being mistaken for real footage, every video and audio clip Genie 4 makes carries an invisible watermark that marks it as AI-generated.Typing a sentence and stepping into the place it describes is, at the moment, something only a handful of testers get to do, two minutes at a time. Google's plan is to widen that circle soon, starting with the people already paying for its top AI plan.
Article Summary: Genie 4 is coming to paying subscribers first, and it still has rough edges. Unlike a game, nothing here was designed beforehand. There are no ready-made levels or characters waiting to be found. Everything you see is created the moment you look at it.

Article Title: Roblox accused of scraping 145GB of 3D files for AI training, adult content included; 3D modelling site says: As far as our logs show, nobody…
Article Text:
(Image via: Roblox)

Update: This story has been updated with a statement from

Roblox

.

Original story follows

What happened

What Roblox has to say

Kids gaming platform Roblox has been accused of scrapping 145GB of 3D files for training artificial intelligence (AI). Independent 3D modeling community Open3DLab shared a blog post where it alleged that a crawler that “belonged to Roblox walked through almost every project on Open3DLab, SFMLab and SmutBase, and proceeded to download complete copies of 1,027 files from 712 projects. 145.5 GB of our creators' work, downloaded for what we assume are AI training purposes”. The crawler used trellis2-data-sourcing/1.0 (3D foundation model research; [redacted]@roblox.com) as its user agent, with the data coming from a single Amazon AWS address.“We want to be careful here. We don't think Roblox set out to collect adult content, and we have no evidence that any of it reached a model or a product. The scrapes were likely automated. But that is exactly the problem: as far as our logs show, nobody checked. A crawler working for a company whose platform tens of millions of children use was pointed at an adult site, and it took explicit models without telling them apart from anything else,” the blog post reads.On Sunday, 18th of October, Open3DLab says it noticed a crawler making a large number of requests to sites and download infrastructure. The crawler sent the same user agent on every request, trellis2-data-sourcing/1.0 (3D foundation model research; [redacted]@roblox.com).It came from a single Amazon Web Services (AWS) address. It had read the main page of 18,926 projects, which is practically the 3D modeling community’s entire catalogue, in 26,429 requests over a span of 34 hours.After pulling the project pages, it downloaded complete copies of 1,027 files from 712 projects, 145.5 GB in all, before suspending operations during the weekend. The downloads include 364 files (54.8 GB) from 224 projects on SmutBase, which hosts adult content only. With the SFMLab projects marked adult, 345 of the 712 projects (62.6 GB) are adult content.The main limiting factor in the number of files downloaded was the crawler's reliance on the free download servers, which have caps on speed limit and number of concurrent downloads. The crawler did not respect robots.txt, (which it did retrieve), ignored Terms of Service, (which forbid scraping), and defied the creators' licenses: 423 of the 712 projects are licensed for non-commercial use only. Within the sample it retrieved, it took adult projects at the same rate as everything else. Some examples include models of Eve from Stellar Blade, Mei from Overwatch, and a Horse cock dildo.The 3D lab says that after detecting the crawler on October 18, it “blocked further attempts the same morning”.Roblox reached out to TOI Tech with a statement.“A Roblox researcher built an agent to collect publicly available 3D assets that mistakenly scraped content from Open3DLab, failing to operate as intended. The agent was decommissioned and the data was not used for any purpose, including training any AI models. We are strengthening safeguards for how agents like this are built and reviewed, and will continue to do so as the agentic landscape evolves,” Roblox spokesperson told TOI Tech.
Article Summary: Roblox accused of scraping 145GB of 3D files for training artificial intelligence (AI) Independent 3D modeling community Open3DLab shared a blog post where it alleged that a crawler that ‘belonged to Roblox’ downloaded 1,027 files from 712 projects’ The downloads include 364 files from 224 projects on SmutBase, which hosts adult content only.

Article Title: IIT Kharagpur highlights success of Nagar Udyam initiative through campus pilot
Article Text: The Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Kharagpur has highlighted the success of its Nagar Udyam initiative that was launched as a pilot within the campus during Durga Puja this year.This is a pioneering solar-powered smart street vending initiative, conceptualised by Prof. Suman Chakraborty, Director, IIT Kharagpur, through its SETU Cloud Kitchen Connect.The aim is to popularise the concept among micro-entrepreneurs, allowing them to do business in a sustainable manner.This model allows a business to start without renting a shop, building permanent infrastructure or occupying roadside space after working hours.It enables an entrepreneur to take an entire business home at night and move it towards customers the next morning.Apart from Prof. Chakraborty, Siddharth Singh Dangi, SDPO, Kharagpur and several others, including small entrepreneurs, were present during the inauguration of the project. This is part of the institute's Platinum Jubilee commitment to translate design and technology into tangible social and economic opportunities.The project involves a small three-wheeled cart that can be towed by the owner's motorcycle. This will enable the entrepreneur to move to where there is demand. It has a range of about 30 km, subject to operational and road-safety validation.Once the day's business is done, the home-storage unit can be taken home, thereby clearing up public road space. The cart has solar-cum-battery renewal-energy-enabled essential low-power functions, with compact battery storage.The carts have the SETU digital backbone, including QR-enabled identification, cashless payments, training and pathways to financial inclusion. They also have built-in hygiene, with protected food display, food-grade surfaces and three-way waste segregation.Through the campus demonstration, IIT Kharagpur hopes to replicate the model across West Bengal, allowing street vendors to operate with dignity, without getting into trouble with the authorities.The compact vending structure can be towed by the owner behind a motorcycle, positioned at suitable places of concentrated demand and taken back home after business hours.A vendor could potentially cater to commuters in one part of the day and to a campus or community gathering later, without being tied to a costly permanent storefront. Its proposed mobility over roughly 30 kilometres offers a route to wider customer access.This changes the equation for both livelihoods and urban space. Rather than treating the entrepreneur’s business and pedestrian accessibility as competing priorities, the design aims for flexible, appropriately authorised vending that does not permanently claim a portion of the road.Further envisaged elements include food-safety status access, grievance redressal and data-assisted governance.“Our ambition is not simply to redesign a street cart; it is to redesign the opportunity around the person who runs it. A business that can move with demand, return home at night and connect to clean energy and digital finance can turn an opportunity seeker into a job creator. That is the kind of technology translation IIT Kharagpur stands for," Prof Chakraborty had said during the launch.The initiative suggests a fresh approach to public-space management: vending with clearer identification, better food practices, mobility and reduced permanent obstruction. These benefits will depend on practical traffic safeguards, lawful operating locations and coordination with civic authorities.As stated by Shri Siddharth Singh Dangi, SDPO, Kharagpur, “The best solutions for our streets must protect livelihoods as well as public safety. A mobile, identifiable and responsibly operated vending unit offers an interesting way to reduce permanent obstruction while preserving economic opportunity. The key will be disciplined implementation, safe movement and compliance with local rules.”The launch at the IIT Kharagpur campus evaluated food safety, operational efficiency, environmental performance, mobility, vendor experience and consumer response.Evidence from the pilot is intended to inform a prospective West Bengal Smart Street Vendor Framework, covering cart standards, food-safety practices, space management and measurable social outcomes. In this micro-startup vision, someone who cannot afford a permanent shop may still be able to build a business — and, over time, create jobs for others.
Article Summary: Nagar Udyam is a pioneering solar-powered smart street vending initiative. The aim is to popularise the concept among micro-entrepreneurs. This model allows a business to start without renting a shop, building permanent infrastructure or occupying roadside space after working hours.

Article Title: Capgemini raises its guidance for second time in 2026; sends strong signal: Rush to use AI is ...
Article Text:
Representative Image

Capgemini CEO on raising guidance

How Capgemini performed across geographies

How business verticals performed

Headcount at CapGemini

One of Europe's biggest IT consulting company Capgemini has ‌raised its 2026 guidance for the second time this year. French IT company raised its guidance after its third-quarter revenue grew 12%, in what is being viewed as the strongest signal yet that the rush to deploy AI is ⁠turning into contracts for Europe's established IT consultancy companies. In earnings call, Capgemini CEO Aiman Ezzat said that third-quarter growth beat analyst expectations and outpaced the sector, with demand now concentrated in overhauling clients' data systems to adapt their business to AI.The Capgemini Group reported third quarter 2026 revenues of €6,073 million, up +12.6% at current exchange rates and +11.7% at constant exchange rates. Capgemini Group CEO Ezzat said that the company continues to see strong momentum in North America and the United Kingdom, and a clear acceleration in France. The Group’s underlying growth (i.e. excluding the impact of acquisitions) in Q3 2026 was solid, supported by the positive momentum in North America and the United Kingdom, as well as continued improvements in France and the Rest of Europe. Acquisitions (notably WNS and Cloud4C closed in Q4 2025) had a material contribution to growth in the North America, United Kingdom & Ireland and Asia-Pacific regions."Our strategy, focused on the new value pools created by AI, is translating into tangible business traction.Clients are now focused on deploying AI at enterprise scale, while addressing challenges related to governance, cost and security. This is driving demand for the modernization of their technology and data foundations, the critical prerequisite for the agentic enterprise. At the same time, clients are transforming their business operations with agentic AI, as reflected in another quarter of double-digit like-for-like growth in Intelligent Business Operations, strengthened by WNS’s scale and capabilities. We are also capturing opportunities in the defense sector and around sovereignty, as clients place greater emphasis on control and strategic resilience," he said.On raising the company's guidance second time this year, Capgemini Group CEO Ezzat said, "Capgemini is uniquely positioned to make AI real for its clients, combining technology, deep industry expertise, business transformation and operational execution, and increasingly leveraging an expanded partner ecosystem. We expect to maintain this momentum and target, on a higher comparison basis, a constant currency growth of 3% to 4% in Q4. On the strength of this quarter, we are raising our 2026 revenue growth target to +9.0% to +9.5% at constant exchange rates, while confirming our operating margin and organic free cash flow objectives.”The Group reported revenues of €6,073 million in Q3 2026, up +12.6% year-on-year. Excluding the +0.9% tailwind from currency fluctuations, constant currency growth* was +11.7%, reflecting underlying growth complemented by the contribution of WNS and Cloud4C. With bookings of €5,401 million in Q3, up +3.4% year-on-year at constant exchange rates, the Capgemini Group demonstrated good commercial momentum.In Q3 2026 and at constant exchange rates, revenues in North America (29% of 2025 Group revenues) grew +18.3% year-on-year, led by continued momentum in Financial Services, alongside strong performances in Manufacturing and Consumer Goods & Retail. The United Kingdom and Ireland region (13% of 2025 Group revenues) posted revenue growth of +25.2% with strong traction in the Public Sector and a very dynamic Consumer Goods & Retail sector while TMT declined.France (19% of 2025 Group revenues) continued its recovery, with revenues up by +4.9% year-on-year. Growth was primarily driven by Manufacturing and Financial Services, even as the Public Sector remained weak.Revenues in the Rest of Europe region (30% of 2025 Group revenues) rose by +3.4%. The Public, Energy & Utilities and Services sectors all grew strongly, and Manufacturing turned slightly positive. Finally, revenues in the Asia-Pacific and Latin America region (9% of 2025 Group revenues) increased +11.9%, supported by the contribution of WNS and Cloud4C, with good growth in the Financial Services and Consumer Goods & Retail sectors.At constant exchange rates, Strategy & Transformation (8% of 2025 Group revenues) reported +18.6% growth in total revenues in Q3 2026. This strong performance reflects the growing demand for business transformation in the era of agentic AI, as clients redesign their enterprise processes around AI.Applications & Technology (63% of 2025 Group revenues and Capgemini’s core business) reported total revenue growth of +3.5%, supported by continued demand for the modernization of legacy technologies, a critical prerequisite for building the new agentic technology stack.Finally, total revenues in Operations & Engineering (29% of 2025 Group revenues) increased +26.9%, with double-digit growth on a like-for-like basis in Intelligent Business Operations, with strong performance across Capgemini and WNS activities.As of September 30, 2026, the Group’s total headcount stood at 417,500, up 62,800 or +18% year-on-year, primarily reflecting the integration of WNS team members, and down 5,900 compared to the end of 2025. The onshore workforce was 141,900 employees. The offshore workforce was 275,600 employees, stable at 66% of the total headcount compared to the end of 2025.
Article Summary: The Capgemini Group reported third quarter 2026 revenues of €6,073 million, up +12.6% at current exchange rates and +11.7% at constant exchange rates. Acquisitions (notably WNS and Cloud4C closed in Q4 2025) had a material contribution to growth in North America, United Kingdom & Ireland and Asia- Pacific regions.

Article Title: Tesla Bull Larry Goldberg wrote a long open letter to Bernie Sanders and everyone who say that Elon Musk is the face of everything wrong with billionaires, days later Spacex CEO responds
Article Text:
Elon Musk has a 'failure warning' for these technology companies; says: Investors have already started betting against them

Here's Larry Goldberg's open letter on Elon Musk

Popularly known as Tesla Bull, Larry Goldberg is an entrepreneur and investor. He is also co-author of the book 'The Decision Model'. Goldberg has started around 20 companies over the years, and sold his first software company at the dotcom peak in 1999. Early last month, Goldberg wrote a long open letter to everyone who he wrote say that Elon Musk is the face of everything wrong with billionaires.Days later, Elon Musk quoted his letter on X, and claimed how Tesla and Spacex have created wealth for their employees over the years. "Tesla and SpaceX have created meaningful wealth for hundreds of thousands of employees over time and improved the retirement savings of hundreds of millions of people," he wrote.Whenever Bernie Sanders and others on the left hold Elon up as the face of everything wrong with billionaires they omit some very pertinent facts: about 158,500 people draw a paycheck directly from one of Elon Musk's companies today, and by my estimate those companies will support roughly 870,000 jobs by the end of this year once you count the suppliers who make their parts and the local businesses where their workers spend their wages.By 2031, in my base case, that number climbs to about 1.4 million.Behind those figures are families making mortgage payments, putting kids through school and building careers in Austin, Brownsville, Fremont, Buffalo, Memphis and dozens, if not hundreds of other places in the US and around the world: they deserve a seat in the conversation.People will argue about wealth and taxes all day. My answer to the criticism is the arithmetic, so I went through the company filings and state records and counted the jobs as carefully as I could.Who works there todayThe direct count is about 158,500. Tesla reported 134,785 employees at the end of 2025 in its 10-K. SpaceX, which now includes xAI and X, reported more than 22,000 full-time employees at March 31 in its S-1 and has added roughly 350 more with Cursor since then. The Boring Company and Neuralink add about 1,350 between them, which is an estimate from LinkedIn-based trackers because neither company publishes headcount. I treat the total as a floor, since Tesla and SpaceX have both kept hiring since those filing dates.Looking out to the end of 2031, my base case reaches about 248,000 direct employees, with a low case near 171,000 and a high case around 377,000. Everything below the company level is my own estimate, built program by program to add up to the filed totals.Where the jobs areTexas is the center of gravity. Giga Texas had 16,506 workers in 2025 according to Travis County's compliance report, and Elon has said Tesla's Austin workforce will likely pass 30,000 by 2028. Starbase near Brownsville had about 4,200 SpaceX employees in March, local officials say the company plans to reach about 8,000 within 18 months, and Cameron County officials credit SpaceX with supporting more than 24,000 jobs in the area. Bastrop's Starlink factory had 1,590 workers in May, and there is a lot more coming behind it, including 3,000 jobs in the first phase of Terafab in Grimes County under the governor's announcement, 9,712 permanent jobs at full operation in the filing for Tesla's Fort Bend solar factory, 1,500 at the Brookshire Megafactory by 2028 and about 250 at the Robstown lithium refinery.The rest of the country has its own long list. Nevada's audited state reports show 7,283 Tesla employees at Gigafactory 1 at an average wage of $48.24 an hour, and the new Semi factory there just entered volume production. Fremont in California is reported at 20,000 to 22,000 workers, and Hawthorne builds Falcon rockets, Dragon capsules, Raptor engines and Starlink terminals. Tesla's Buffalo plant had 2,399 full-time workers at the end of 2025, with another 1,060 elsewhere in New York. In Memphis, xAI says it employs almost 3,000 people locally, a count that runs from electricians and engineers to cooks and construction workers, and Mississippi expects hundreds of permanent jobs from the more than $20 billion xAI is investing in Southaven. Florida's Starship deal carries at least 600 new jobs by 2030 on top of the hundreds SpaceX already employs at the Cape. Louisiana expects 3,000 direct jobs at Starbase Louisiana over ten years at an average salary of $92,600, and projects about 34,500 construction jobs at the peak of the build.The footprint reaches well beyond the US. Shanghai's last reported figure was about 20,000 workers in 2023, and Berlin is hiring back to about 12,700 people in vehicle production, with more than 1,500 further hires planned for its new battery cell plant.Where the growth comes fromRobotaxi operations are the single biggest addition in my base case, at roughly 16,750 people covering the depots, remote support and fleet care that a large autonomous fleet needs. Tesla's sales, service, engineering and corporate base adds about 11,300 as the fleet on the road roughly doubles, and Optimus adds about 10,600 if Fremont reaches a million robots a year. After that come vehicle manufacturing including Cybercab at about 6,700, battery cells at about 6,000, Fort Bend solar at about 5,800, Starbase Texas at about 4,900 and Terafab at about 2,900. Starbase Louisiana only reaches about 1,200 direct jobs by 2031, since construction starts next year and the first launch is 2029 at the earliest.To be fair about it, the low case is nearly flat, because Optimus and factory automation offset most of the new hiring. Even in the base case, productivity gains keep vehicle manufacturing far below the roughly 106,000 workers that kind of volume would otherwise take. I count that as a strength, because companies that keep getting more productive are the ones that can keep growing and keep paying well, and the next section shows why the wider job count keeps rising even when factory headcount doesn't.The wider footprintEvery one of these factories, launch sites and data centers buys parts, materials and services, and every paycheck gets spent at local businesses. Using the Economic Policy Institute's 2019 multipliers, which separate supplier jobs from jobs supported by worker spending, I estimate the companies' end-2026 workforce supports roughly 870,000 jobs in all once both layers are added to the direct staff. By 2031 that reaches about 0.93 million in the low case, 1.41 million in the base case and 2.27 million in the high case. Supplier jobs follow output, so a factory that makes more with fewer people keeps buying more parts and materials, which is why this total grows even in the low case. Worker-spending jobs follow headcount, since they come out of payroll.I'd hold these wider numbers more loosely than the direct ones, and the right way to describe them is jobs supported by Musk-company spending, since these suppliers also work for other customers. The multipliers are US national averages, so they overstate the effect of Shanghai and Berlin, where about half of Tesla's vehicle workforce sits. At US multipliers that group alone accounts for about 243,000 of the end-2026 supplier and spending jobs, and most of those would really be in China and Germany. The data center supplier figure is probably on the high side as well, and temporary construction work is a separate layer that isn't in any of these totals.The bottom lineElon's critics are entitled to their view of billionaires, but the numbers still matter. About 158,500 people work directly for his companies today, and if robotaxi, Optimus, chips and solar ramp roughly on plan, that could reach about 250,000 by 2031. Counting suppliers and worker spending, those companies will support roughly 870,000 jobs by the end of this year and about 1.4 million by 2031 in my base case, spread across Texas, Louisiana, Nevada, Florida, California, New York, Tennessee, Mississippi and factories around the world. That is a lot of American families, and plenty more beyond our borders, whose livelihoods are tied to what Elon builds.
Article Summary: Larry Goldberg is an entrepreneur and investor. He has started around 20 companies over the years, and sold his first software company at the dotcom peak in 1999. He wrote a long open letter to everyone who he wrote say that Elon Musk is the face of everything wrong with billionaires. His answer to the criticism is the arithmetic, so he counted the jobs as carefully as he could.

Article Title: Jeff Bezos commits $100 million to a $500 million wildlife alliance targeting 31,000 endangered species as global conservation funding falls short
Article Text:
Bezos Earth Fund backs $500 million alliance to protect endangered species

More than 31,000 species fall within the alliance’s target categories

Earlier Phoenix project targets 100 species across 30 countries

Government nature funding remains below international targets

Bezos Earth Fund has distributed $2.4 billion of its $10 billion pledge

Thousands of animal and plant species are at risk of disappearing, and conservation groups often need years of uninterrupted work to bring vulnerable populations back from the brink. Jeff Bezos and Lauren Sánchez Bezos are backing a new international effort that aims to give some of those projects more dependable financial support. As reported by Fortune, The Bezos Earth Fund has committed $100 million to the Species Recovery Alliance, a partnership involving 9 founding organisations and a combined $500 million commitment. Announced during a United Nations biodiversity summit in Armenia in October 2026, the initiative will support conservation programmes for species facing some of the highest risks of extinction.The Species Recovery Alliance was announced on 16 October at the Leaders’ Summit of COP17, the United Nations biodiversity conference held in Yerevan, Armenia. The Bezos Earth Fund is among 9 founding members, with its contribution accounting for $100 million of the initiative’s $500 million commitment, according to a spokesperson quoted by Fortune.The partnership brings together organisations with different conservation interests, including Re:wild, the environmental group co-founded by Leonardo DiCaprio, and Rainforest Trust.The other founding members are the Colossal Foundation, Critical Ecosystem Partnership Fund, Fondation Segré, Franklinia Foundation, Ayers Wild Cat Conservation Trust and WildLives Earth.Rather than placing all the money in one shared pot, the members will manage their own grants while coordinating their work. Funding is intended for conservation organisations and local partners tackling threats to species classified by the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) as endangered, critically endangered or extinct in the wild.Cristián Samper, managing director of the Bezos Earth Fund and its nature solutions lead, said a lack of dependable funding could put recovery efforts at risk even after conservation teams had made substantial progress.The IUCN Red List identifies more than 49,500 species as threatened with extinction. The new alliance will concentrate on three high-risk categories, which together cover more than 31,000 species.Its funding could support a range of interventions, depending on what each species needs. Some programmes may involve breeding animals in captivity before releasing them into the wild. Others may focus on rebuilding damaged habitats, reducing the spread of disease or controlling invasive species that threaten native wildlife.The alliance intends to track progress through the IUCN Red List and its Green Status of Species, which provides a way to assess conservation outcomes and the recovery of species over time.The new alliance follows another major commitment by the Bezos Earth Fund and Re:wild. In August 2026, the two organisations launched the Phoenix Species Project, pledging $100 million each towards a combined $200 million effort. That programme aims to recover 100 critically endangered species and species already extinct in the wild across 30 countries. Its targets include Madagascar’s golden-crowned sifaka, a rare lemur, and Australia’s elusive night parrot.The Phoenix initiative and the Species Recovery Alliance are separate efforts, although both involve the Bezos Earth Fund and an emphasis on reversing severe declines in wildlife populations.Lauren Sánchez Bezos, the fund’s vice chair, described the Phoenix project as a response to the possibility that children could grow up without ever encountering some of the animals that fascinate them. Her comments drew attention to a less visible aspect of extinction: species can disappear before future generations have a chance to know they existed.Private philanthropy is taking on a larger role as governments struggle to meet their biodiversity commitments. At the 2022 United Nations biodiversity summit in Montreal, countries agreed to mobilise $200 billion annually for biodiversity by 2030.Figures from the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development, cited by the Associated Press, put annual funding at between $75 billion and $92 billion from 2023 to 2025. That leaves a substantial gap between the money being raised and the level countries agreed to pursue. A United Nations progress report issued ahead of the October summit also found that fewer than half of national biodiversity targets were on track.Astrid Schomaker, executive secretary of the UN Convention on Biological Diversity, told the Associated Press that progress was not happening quickly enough. Alongside the private-sector alliance, 17 governments led by Colombia and Armenia launched a separate initiative known as the Coalition of Action to Recover Endangered Species, or CARES. The two efforts have different structures, but both seek to strengthen action on species facing extinction.Jeff Bezos established the Bezos Earth Fund in 2020 with a pledge of $10 billion to support climate action and nature conservation by 2030. The commitment was presented as the largest individual philanthropic pledge focused on climate and nature at the time.The fund has distributed $2.4 billion so far, a spokesperson told Fortune. More than $7 billion therefore remains to be allocated over the roughly four years leading up to the deadline. Fund officials told Bloomberg in May 2026 that they remained committed to the target.The latest species recovery commitment is part of a broader programme of grants. In recent months, the fund has announced $34 million for sustainable fabrics, $26 million for wildfire detection and $100 million for turning vacant urban land into parks in eight US cities. In September, it also announced more than $25 million in grants connected to the Pacific Ocean.
Article Summary: The Bezos Earth Fund has committed $100 million to the Species Recovery Alliance, a partnership involving 9 founding organisations and a combined $500 million commitment. The initiative will support conservation programmes for species facing some of the highest risks of extinction. The new alliance will concentrate on three high-risk categories, which together cover more than 31,000 species.

Article Title: Microsoft's ex-lawyer, and now Washington Governor, is angry with the company; says: I love the company, but 'what's up with ...'
Article Text:
Representative Image

What Microsoft ad says that made Governor 'upset'

What Washington Governor told Seattle Metropolitan Chamber of Commerce

Washington Governor Bob Ferguson is reportedly not happy with Microsoft. According to a report by GeekWire, Ferguson took aim at Microsoft over a political action committee's ad campaign criticizing the State government, speaking during what was intended to be an off-the-record business summit. Leaked audio obtained from the Seattle Metropolitan Chamber of Commerce’s Regional Leadership Conference at the Suncadia resort shows Ferguson directly challenging the software giant. The audio was originally published by independent state politics newsletter The Washington Observer.At issue is an ad funded by Washington Needs to Compete, a PAC that state campaign finance records show has raised roughly $13.8 million -- including over $5 million directly from Microsoft, alongside contributions from CEO Satya Nadella, former CEO Steve Ballmer, and President Brad Smith. Other corporate donors include T-Mobile, F5, Alaska Airlines and Weyerhaeuser.The commercial reportedly targets the State capital, claiming that “Olympia is broken, spending more while you get less,” and features a line that particularly irked the governor: “In Washington, it used to be all you needed was an idea, a dream and the guts to chase it.”As reported by GeekWire, Microsoft ad opens with a nod to “inventors in garages,” “mom-and-pop shops down Main Street” and farmers “feeding the world,” before declaring, “In Washington, it used to be all you needed was an idea, a dream and the guts to chase it.”Then it turns, says: "But today, Olympia is broken, spending more while you get less." Jobs are leaving, the ad says, and “it’s harder than ever to afford a home and raise a family.” The ad, however, does not name Ferguson or any legislation. It ends by saying Olympia needs to "quit wasting money, fix what’s broken and put Washington families first."According to GeekWire, Ferguson repeated the words “it used to be” in disbelief before pressing the room of business and civic leaders. “What’s up with that?” Ferguson asked. “First, does anyone else in this room believe that? I sure as hell don’t.”Defending the state’s business climate, Ferguson cited PitchBook figures showing Seattle-area startups raised a record $3.5 billion in the third quarter—more than triple the amount from the same period a year earlier.The governor, a former Microsoft attorney who emphasized his respect for the company, voiced frustration that the spot aired during high-profile Seattle Seahawks broadcasts, reaching potential founders and transplants across the country. Records cited by GeekWire show the PAC spent $97,000 on an October 15 broadcast on Prime Video and $130,000 during an October 25 NBC telecast.“If we’re partners, partners should treat partners like partners, right?” Ferguson said, asking the audience to picture the backlash if he launched a multimillion-dollar campaign blasting Microsoft. “You guys would think I lost my mind if I did that.”While conceding that the State faces real hurdles, Ferguson urged the executives present to champion Washington’s strengths alongside its challenges, calling the region “so bloody special.” Ferguson, who assumed office in January 2025, also issued a firm reminder about his political horizon: “I plan on being governor for a long time,” he said, noting he intends to continue working with local business leaders, “Microsoft included. ”The Observer reported that Microsoft Olympia representative Michael Mattmiller was present and "kinda-sorta hugged it out afterward" with the governor. The report noted that Mattmiller declined to comment on the newsletter.
Article Summary: Washington Governor Bob Ferguson reportedly took aim at Microsoft over a political action committee's ad campaign criticizing the State government. Leaked audio obtained from the Seattle Metropolitan Chamber of Commerce’s Regional Leadership Conference shows Ferguson directly challenging the software giant. At issue is an ad funded by Washington Needs to Compete, a PAC that state campaign finance records show has raised roughly $13.8 million.

Article Title: ChatGPT to teenagers: We will not answer your queries, how harmless they may be, if you ask about ...
Article Text:
